open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A scan covers the photo folder and all its subfolders (R0-12).
open_points.question: What result is produced when the root or a non-ignored subfolder cannot be listed, disappears during traversal, or has an unreadable directory entry?
options: Refuse the entire scan with `folder_unavailable`
Skip the failed subtree and continue
Report a synthetic rejected observation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the entire scan with `folder_unavailable`.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has a readable photo root containing one readable folder and one subfolder that cannot be listed.
events: The calling flow requests a scan.
The deliverer reaches the unreadable subfolder.
outcomes: The whole scan is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
The unreadable subtree is skipped and observations from the readable folder are returned.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: The earlier file of rule 8 is the first file with that content in this order that reached rule 8.
open_points.question: Does “reached rule 8” mean the first file on which the duplicate check was evaluated, or a file for which rule 8 applied, and can a rejected, settling, placed or published observation be `duplicate_of`?
options: Use the first earlier file that passed rules 1–7
Use only an earlier file already classified `ready`, `placed` or `published`
Use only an earlier file already classified `duplicate`
open_points.default_guess: Use the first earlier file that passed rules 1–7.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or with `~syncthing~`, or ends in `.tmp` or `~`.
open_points.question: Which case-insensitive comparison is required for filesystem names: ASCII-only folding, Unicode simple lowercase, or Unicode casefolding?
options: ASCII-insensitive matching for the ASCII patterns
Unicode casefolding
Platform filesystem case rules
open_points.default_guess: Use ASCII-insensitive matching for the ASCII patterns.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show for INV-01's claim that no operation changes the source folder, including refused, failed and concurrent operations and connection-management operations?
options: Exercise every declared operation and relevant failure path
The four listed successful actions are sufficient
Prove read-only access structurally in addition to the listed test
open_points.default_guess: Require structural proof of read-only source access plus tests of every source-touching operation and its failure paths.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: A stored image is a newly encoded JPEG made from the decoded pixels of the source.
open_points.question: Which exact JPEG encoding choices are required beyond `PHOTO_QUALITY`, including color conversion, chroma subsampling, progressive/baseline mode, optimization and deterministic output?
options: Fix every encoder option and require deterministic bytes
Fix quality only and accept library defaults
Require only the size and metadata invariants, allowing different JPEG bytes
open_points.default_guess: Fix RGB conversion, baseline encoding, subsampling and all encoder options explicitly so the result is deterministic.

witness.initial: A source image has saturated color detail and produces different sizes under common JPEG subsampling defaults.
events: One implementation encodes at quality 85 with 4:2:0 subsampling.
Another encodes at quality 85 with 4:4:4 subsampling.
outcomes: The image fits the output limit and is placed.
The image exceeds the output limit and fails with `too_large`.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` with `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`, EXIF `DateTime`, then the file's modification time.
open_points.question: What exact date grammar and offset ranges make an EXIF value usable, and what happens to `DateTimeOriginal` when its offset is absent, invalid or out of range?
options: Accept only the EXIF date grammar and valid UTC offsets, then fall back to `DateTime`
Use `DateTimeOriginal` without an offset in the configured time zone
Accept any parser-supported datetime and offset
open_points.default_guess: Accept strict EXIF date syntax and valid UTC offsets; otherwise fall back to `DateTime`, then modification time.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: INV-03: a stored image carries no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comment of its source.
open_points.question: Does the product constraint that nothing but pixels reaches the store also prohibit ICC profiles, IPTC data, thumbnails and other JPEG application segments, and what must the invariant test inspect?
options: Strip every source-derived metadata/application segment, including ICC and IPTC
Strip only EXIF, GPS, XMP and comments
Preserve color profiles but strip identifying metadata
open_points.default_guess: Strip all source-derived metadata and application segments; encode solely from normalized pixels.

witness.initial: A JPEG contains no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comment but contains an ICC profile and embedded thumbnail.
events: The file is placed.
One implementation copies the ICC profile while another encodes only pixels.
outcomes: The stored JPEG contains the source ICC profile.
The stored JPEG contains no source metadata at all.
witness.observer: A client downloading the image and a security reviewer

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: A requested source with no placement that this scan does not report as `ready` fails with `not_ready_or_absent`.
open_points.question: When several paths have the requested content hash and one is `ready` while the others are `duplicate`, which path supplies the placement's `name` and bytes?
options: Use the first `ready` observation in traversal order
Treat the hash as ambiguous and fail
Allow any matching path
open_points.default_guess: Use the first `ready` observation in traversal order.

witness.initial: Files `a.jpg` and `b.jpg` have identical bytes, so `a.jpg` is `ready` and `b.jpg` is `duplicate`.
events: The calling flow requests placement using their shared source hash.
outcomes: The placement records `a.jpg` as its name.
The placement records `b.jpg` or refuses the ambiguous hash.
witness.observer: The calling flow reading the stored placement

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: Checks run in this order: token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, every source id.
open_points.question: What exact response status and refusal payload are used for an invalid request form, invalid project UUID, invalid item count, malformed source id, unavailable connection data and unavailable folder?
options: Define a refusal code and HTTP status for every failed check
Use framework validation responses for form and UUID failures and domain refusals for the rest
Use one generic bad-request refusal
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit HTTP status and stable refusal payload for every check, preserving this precedence.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: A malformed source id refuses the whole call before anything is written.
open_points.question: How does whole-call refusal for one malformed source id agree with State 0's rule “A failed photo does not stop the others” and “a bad file is reported on its own and the others proceed”?
options: Malformed identifiers are request failures, not failed photos, and must be explicitly excluded from the State 0 rule
Every malformed source id becomes an item failure and other items proceed
Every item failure refuses the whole call
open_points.default_guess: State explicitly that malformed identifiers invalidate the request, while failures of validly identified photos remain per-item.

witness.initial: A placement request contains one valid source id followed by one malformed source id.
events: The owner submits the two selected entries in one call.
outcomes: State 2 refuses the entire call and writes nothing.
State 0's per-photo rule allows the valid photo to be placed and reports only the malformed entry as failed.

open_points.subject: A4
open_points.text: A `photo_id` is a UUID, kept in lowercase hyphenated form.
open_points.question: Must input already be lowercase hyphenated text, or are other valid UUID spellings accepted and canonicalized, and which refusal results from an invalid spelling?
options: Accept any valid UUID spelling and canonicalize it
Accept only lowercase hyphenated UUID text
Let framework parsing decide
open_points.default_guess: Accept any valid UUID spelling, canonicalize to lowercase hyphenated form, and define the invalid-input refusal.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: The token is generated with 256 bits from a cryptographic random source and is kept in a UTF-8 file.
open_points.question: Which textual encoding and exact length represent the 256-bit token in the UTF-8 file and in the Bearer header?
options: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
Unpadded base64url
Padded base64
Any lossless UTF-8 encoding
open_points.default_guess: Use 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

witness.initial: A deployment needs a new token.
events: One operator uses a 64-character hexadecimal token.
Another uses a 43-character unpadded base64url token.
outcomes: Clients send a hexadecimal Bearer token.
Clients send a base64url Bearer token.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: The service does not start when the group or others have any permission on the file or the token has fewer than 32 characters.
open_points.question: Must the token path also be a regular non-symlink file owned by the service account, and what happens for invalid UTF-8, an unreadable file, multiple lines, or a token consisting partly or wholly of trimmed whitespace?
options: Require a regular non-symlink owner-readable file with valid UTF-8 and one nonblank token
Enforce only mode bits and post-trim length
Follow symlinks and let ordinary I/O or decoding errors determine startup
open_points.default_guess: Require a regular non-symlink file owned by the service account, valid UTF-8, and exactly one post-trim token meeting the length rule.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: Any other value is refused with 401 before the request's identifiers or body are examined.
open_points.question: What is the compared value when a request contains zero, two, or more `Authorization` headers, or a header with leading/trailing whitespace?
options: Require exactly one header whose raw value exactly matches
Use the web framework's combined or selected value
Trim HTTP whitespace before exact comparison
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one header and compare its value exactly.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: A project id must be a UUID and a source id 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
open_points.question: Which UUID textual forms are accepted for a project id, and are source ids validated before or after UUID canonicalization and connection lookup?
options: Accept and canonicalize all valid UUID text
Require lowercase hyphenated UUID text
Use framework-dependent UUID parsing
open_points.default_guess: Accept valid UUID text, canonicalize it before lookup, and require source ids to match exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none.
open_points.question: How are temporary names made collision-safe, with what permissions are they created, and what removes abandoned temporary files after a crash?
options: Use exclusive random temporary files with final permissions and clean stale files on recovery
Use a fixed deterministic temporary name under the project lock
Leave abandoned temporary files permanently
open_points.default_guess: Use exclusive unpredictable names, set the required mode before publication, and safely clean recognized stale temporary files during recovery.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: A caller waits for the lock without a time limit, and the lock is released when its holder ends.
open_points.question: Is the operation's sole clock reading taken before waiting for the project lock or after acquiring it, and which instant is the operation meant to represent?
options: Read after acquiring the lock and immediately before checking state/files
Read before waiting for the lock
Read at HTTP request receipt
open_points.default_guess: Read after acquiring the lock and before inspecting state or source files.

witness.initial: Another process holds the project lock for ten minutes.
events: A mark request is accepted and waits for the lock.
The lock becomes available and the mark is written.
outcomes: `marked_at` records the time before the ten-minute wait.
`marked_at` records the time after the lock is acquired.
witness.observer: The owner reading the publication mark

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: Scan, placement and mark each read it once, after the request is accepted and before any file is examined.
open_points.question: Does the scan performed inside a placement share the placement's one reading, or does it count as a scan that takes an additional reading?
options: The placement call and its internal scan share one reading
The placement takes one reading and its internal scan takes another
Placement delegates all timing to its internal scan and takes no separate reading
open_points.default_guess: The placement call and its internal scan share exactly one reading.

witness.initial: A source file is close to the settling boundary.
events: A placement call is accepted.
The placement performs its required internal scan.
outcomes: One clock read is used for both placement and scan.
Two clock reads occur and the second can change the file from settling to ready.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the counting-clock test

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no rounding, written in ISO 8601 form.
open_points.question: Which exact ISO 8601 spelling is required: separator, fixed or omitted fractional digits, and whether a `Z` or offset is forbidden?
options: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with no suffix
Variable ISO 8601 fractional precision with no suffix
A `Z` suffix for UTC
open_points.default_guess: Use `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with exactly six fractional digits and no suffix.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered.
open_points.question: How is a filesystem modification time with nanosecond precision converted to microseconds while also satisfying “no rounding,” and is the same converted value used for settling and the delivered fallback date?
options: Truncate sub-microsecond digits and reuse that value everywhere
Round to the nearest microsecond
Compare at native precision but serialize at microsecond precision
open_points.default_guess: Truncate to microseconds once and use that value for both comparison and delivery.

witness.initial: A file's modification time is 100.9999999 seconds and the settling boundary differs within the discarded nanoseconds.
events: A scan converts and compares the modification time.
outcomes: Truncation makes the file old enough and `ready`.
Native-precision comparison leaves it `settling`.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy` and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.
open_points.question: What observable result is required if `utc_now` fails or returns a non-UTC, offset-bearing, or lower-precision value?
options: Refuse the whole operation with a defined service error
Normalize valid offset-bearing values and reject invalid values
Allow the backend exception to become an unspecified server error
open_points.default_guess: Validate the clock result and fail the entire operation with a defined internal-service refusal before examining files or writing state.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: INV-13: one operation uses one reading of the service clock.
open_points.question: Does INV-13 cover health answers and refused requests, which rule 2 says use zero readings, and does its Required tests item have to show zero reads for refused requests and one read for replayed marks?
options: Rewrite the invariant to distinguish accepted timed operations from health and refusals, and test every case
Interpret “one operation” as only scan, accepted placement and accepted mark
Require one read even for health and refused requests
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite INV-13 to say that every accepted scan, placement and mark uses exactly one reading, while health and refused requests use none; test replayed marks and representative refusals explicitly.

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: `RefusalCode` is `unknown_project`, `connection_not_confirmed`, `folder_unavailable`, `invalid_source_id`, `unsafe_reference`, `not_placed` and `publication_conflict`.
open_points.question: What exact condition produces `unsafe_reference`, how does it differ from `folder_unavailable` and `invalid_source_id`, and at what position in each operation's check order is it evaluated?
options: Use it for a generated or persisted binary reference that escapes `binary_root`
Use it for any source or folder path traversal attempt
Remove it because all unsafe paths are already represented by other refusals
open_points.default_guess: Use `unsafe_reference` when a stored-image reference resolves outside `binary_root`, checked before any read or write through that reference.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: The direct libraries are pinned to exact versions: pillow, fastapi, pydantic and uvicorn.
open_points.question: What exact version of each library is the accepted dependency decision?
options: State four concrete versions in A9
Delegate versions to a later dependency lock
Use the prototype's current versions
open_points.default_guess: State and review four concrete current versions in A9 rather than silently inheriting the prototype.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: Before each deployment every distribution installed in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, no older than the deploy route's maximum snapshot age.
open_points.question: What is the maximum snapshot age, where is that decided value supplied, and how is snapshot age calculated?
options: Define a provider constant and compare snapshot timestamp to a deployment clock
Make the maximum a deployment configuration field
Require an online OSV query at deployment and eliminate snapshot age
open_points.default_guess: Define an imported policy constant for maximum age and compare against an authenticated snapshot timestamp using the deployment authority's UTC clock.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: Any known vulnerability listed for an installed version blocks the deployment, whatever its severity, and a check that cannot complete does not pass.
open_points.question: Do withdrawn OSV entries, disputed records, aliases, environment markers and vulnerabilities whose ranges cannot be evaluated count as blocking, and what exact result represents an incomplete check?
options: Follow specified OSV semantics and fail closed on unknown evaluation
Block every record mentioning the package/version, including withdrawn entries
Delegate all semantics to whichever scanner is installed
open_points.default_guess: Use OSV's affected-version semantics, ignore formally withdrawn records, and fail closed whenever applicability cannot be determined.

open_points.subject: A11
open_points.text: A `photo_date` ending in `Z` or in an offset `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` is an old date.
open_points.question: What exact input representation is inspected, including lowercase `z`, offsets with seconds, whitespace, parsed datetime values and malformed dates, and what does “only UTC dates passes” mean when `Z` itself denotes UTC?
options: Accept only naive ISO 8601 UTC text as repaired; treat every suffix or malformed value as blocking
Treat `Z` as valid UTC and only nonzero offsets as old
Use the Portal client's datetime parser and inspect whether the parsed value is offset-aware
open_points.default_guess: Treat only well-formed offset-free ISO 8601 UTC values as repaired; block `Z`, all explicit offsets and malformed values.

open_points.subject: A11
open_points.text: Before placing anything for a project, the calling flow reads that project's staff photo list in the Portal.
open_points.question: How does the flow prove it has read the complete list when the Portal paginates, truncates or changes the list during reading?
options: Read every page from a stable snapshot or fail closed
Inspect only the first/default page
Repeat pagination until one pass is unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Require complete stable pagination and fail closed if completeness cannot be established.

witness.initial: A project has more photos than one Portal response page, and an old date exists only on the second page.
events: The calling flow reads the default first page.
The owner requests delivery.
outcomes: The flow sees no old date and publishes a new photo.
The flow reads all pages, detects the old date and publishes nothing.

open_points.subject: A11
open_points.text: The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.
open_points.question: What exact future check must demonstrate INV-17, rather than leaving the test conditional on whether the calling flow exists?
options: Name a required E2E check that asserts zero place and publish calls after an old date or list-read failure
Detection-only tests are sufficient until the flow exists
Remove INV-17 until the flow exists
open_points.default_guess: Require an E2E check that injects an old date and a list-read failure and asserts that neither placement nor publication is called.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: `intake_id` identifies the delivery of one source photo to one project: the deliverer derives it from the placement identity as `deliverer-photo-<project_id>-<first 32 characters of source_id>`, so a repeated publication is recognised by the Portal.
open_points.question: How are two different SHA-256 source ids with the same first 32 characters given distinct Portal publication identities?
options: Use the complete source id in `intake_id`
Prove the truncated identifier is an accepted collision risk and define the resulting behavior
Add a collision-resistant encoding or stored disambiguator
open_points.default_guess: Use the complete source id unless the Portal imposes a length limit; otherwise define a collision-resistant full-hash encoding.

witness.initial: One project has two different source hashes sharing their first 32 hexadecimal characters.
events: The first placement is published with its derived `intake_id`.
The second placement is published with the same derived `intake_id`.
outcomes: The Portal treats the second publication as a replay of the first photo.
The two placements publish as two distinct photos.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: A placed file adds its `file_ref`, a published file adds its Portal `photo_id`, and a duplicate names the earlier file with the same content.
open_points.question: When a second path has content whose placement or mark already exists, does A1 rule 8 classify it as `duplicate` without `file_ref` or `photo_id`, or does the State 1 model require it to be `placed` or `published` with those fields?
options: Duplicate precedence wins and duplicate observations omit placement fields
Placement/publication status wins over duplicate status
Duplicate observations also carry the existing `file_ref` and `photo_id`
open_points.default_guess: Keep duplicate precedence but explicitly state whether the duplicate observation carries the existing placement and mark fields.

witness.initial: `a.jpg` and `b.jpg` have identical content, and that content has already been placed and marked.
events: A scan visits `a.jpg` first and `b.jpg` second.
outcomes: `b.jpg` is `duplicate` because rule 8 precedes `published`.
`b.jpg` is `published` and carries `file_ref` and `photo_id` as the State 1 model description suggests.

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: | `min_age_seconds` | `int` | 120 |
open_points.rule: | константа или таблица политики: пороги, имена, префиксы, закрытые наборы, таблицы правил | константа поставщика данных (§6.10) | `the imported X constant` | имя символа и его тип |
open_points.question: The fixed settling-time threshold must become a data-provider policy constant named to generated code as an imported constant, or the text must establish that it is genuinely an environment-dependent launch setting instead of a decided policy threshold.
